<reason>B wins by separating permission to compete from exemption from shared costs. A raises legitimate financing, enforcement, and transaction-cost concerns, but B answers the pressure directly with retained network contributions, participant-funded backup and upgrades, and binding export limits. A's remaining national-regime objection depends on insufficiently established claims that safeguards will fail or meaningful savings will disappear. B offers the stronger comparison: commercially unsuccessful trades need not proceed, while compliant, worthwhile trades should remain available.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's “Protection is mandatory; profit is conditional” directly undercuts A's harmful-or-pointless dilemma. A subsequently treats B's concession that efficient retailers may eliminate margins in some markets as though it establishes their disappearance generally, without answering B's restricted-purchaser competition mechanism.</best_rebuttal>
